To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
U1 and U1/U6 isoforms can be used to correct splice defects caused by mutations in the splice donor site of the gene BBS (Bardet-Biedl Syndrome) in a minigene assay.

we have identified seven different mutations in the splice donor site of the BBS1 gene that cause a splice defect and that we have designed and tested U1 small nuclear RNAs that correct the splice defect of four mutations.
we developed a gene therapy approach to correct splice errors with modified splice factor snRNPs, and this approach has therapeutic potential for a wide range of splice mutations.

gene therapy for the correction of splicing mutations in monogenetic diseases.
a novel gene therapeutic approach to restore the normal splicing pattern of pre-mRNAs with splice defects caused by mutations in the SD.
the correction of splice defects with modified splicing factors.

we have shown that the splice defect caused by the mutation of the SD can be corrected by mutation adapted U1 and U1+U6 snRNPs.

The main takeaway from our work is that

splice defects caused by mutations at SD positions +4 and +5 can be effectively treated with U1 and U1/U6 combination therapy, whereas splice defects caused by SD mutations at +6 require U1 and U2/U6 combination therapy.
splice defects caused by mutations at SD positions +1, +3, and +7 can be completely corrected.
splice defects caused by mutations in the splice donor site can be corrected by gene therapy.
